title: Longest Word in Dictionary through Deleting
description: Given a lowercase string `s` and an array of lowercase strings `dictionary`, return the longest string in `dictionary` that can be formed by deleting zero or more characters from `s` (i.e., is a subsequence of `s`). If multiple words tie for the longest length, return the lexicographically smallest one; if none qualify, return `""`.
hints: You can test whether word w is a subsequence of s in O(|s|) time with a two-pointer scan.
Only run the subsequence check if w is strictly better than the current best answer (longer, or equal length and lexicographically smaller).

examples.explanation: "ale", "apple", and "plea" are subsequences of "abpcplea", and "apple" is the longest (length 5).
"a", "b", and "c" all have length 1; "a" is lexicographically smallest.
No dictionary word is a subsequence of "xyz", so return "".
